analysis: Testosterone production is primarily carried out by Leydig cells, which are located in the interstitial tissue of the testes. These cells are responsible for synthesizing and secreting testosterone in response to luteinizing hormone (LH) stimulation. Sertoli cells support spermatogenesis but do not produce testosterone, while seminiferous tubules are involved in sperm production. The epididymis is responsible for the maturation and storage of sperm, not hormone production.
